assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epics table: Epic 1 summary is 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', Epic 2 summary is 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both match the required '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention references in Implementation Notes use the prescribed format. Examples: Task 1: 'Per CONVENTIONS.md §Module Pattern: ... Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/mod.rs` matching the convention's module directory scope.' Task 4: 'Per CONVENTIONS.md §API Layer: ... Applies: task modifies `src/api/rest.ts` matching the convention's API client file scope.' Task 5: 'Per CONVENTIONS.md §Component Library: ... Applies: task creates `src/pages/RemediationDashboardPage/RemediationDashboardPage.tsx` matching the convention's `.tsx` component file scope.' No inapplicable conventions are listed with 'Not applicable' annotations. Backend tasks do not include frontend conventions and vice versa. All rationales follow the 'Applies: task modifies/creates <file> matching the convention's <scope>' format.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature priority is 'Major' (from feature-epic-hierarchy.md). impact-map.md Inherited Fields table: 'Priority | Major | Yes | Feature priority is "Major" (not "Undefined"), so it is propagated to all Epics and Tasks'. additional_fields for Task creation includes '"priority": {"name": "Major"}'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Priority | Major | Propagated to all Epics and Tasks (Feature priority is set and not "Undefined")'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature has fixVersions: 'RHTPA 1.5.0' (non-empty). No 'Jira Field Defaults' section in CLAUDE.md, so scope defaults to 'both'. impact-map.md Inherited Fields: 'Fix Versions | RHTPA 1.5.0 | Yes | Feature has non-empty fixVersions; no Jira Field Defaults section exists, so fixVersion scope defaults to "both" — propagated to both Epics and Tasks'. additional_fields for Task creation: '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in outputs directory and contains an 'Inherited Fields' section with a table showing: Priority=Major (Propagated to all Epics and Tasks), Fix Versions=RHTPA 1.5.0 (Propagated to all Epics and Tasks), Labels=ai-generated-jira (Applied to all created issues). impact-map.md also contains a parallel 'Inherited Fields' section with the same information plus rationales.
